setup.why: none needed — free-text q filter on the fixture project's own name resolves it directly

notes: Query-only capability (no path_params, no body, no json_path nesting): q (flat string), p (int, default 1), sort_by (closed enum), starred/shared (bool passthrough), is_hidden_projects (bool). No param is marked required. First probe used q=__mcp-capability-fixture__ and returned exactly the pool's fixture project (id 379335744, identifier PR-2005), so the item shape was genuinely exercised, not an empty-collection case. A second, unfiltered call (p=1, sort_by=identifier-asc) confirmed the paging block: page_size is fixed at 30 regardless of no size param being sent (30 rows returned), count=1832 matches the account's known project total, prev=null and next=2 on page 1 — all consistent with the declared `info` schema (page/page_size/count/prev/next all present and correctly typed). One extra field, info.starred_count, appears in both calls' info block but is not in the declared schema (which lists only the five required fields). At the item level, the declared 200 schema promises `project_creator` (boolean) but it is never emitted by either call — this matches the capability's own guidance text ('project_creator ... is NOT emitted ... commented out in the serializer'), so the omission is self-disclosed rather than surprising, but it is still a genuine declared-vs-actual schema mismatch. Conversely, the actual response carries seven item fields not present in the declared 200 schema object at all (thProjectId, test_plans_count, normalisedName, starred, jira_mapped, projectVisibilityBanner, duplicates_tc_count) plus info.starred_count; most of these (thProjectId, normalisedName, starred, jira_mapped, test_plans_count, duplicates_tc_count, projectVisibilityBanner) are at least named in the capability's flat `returns` manifest and/or guidance prose, but none of them are represented in the structured response.schema.200 object that describeCapability hands back as 'the declared 200 response'. Net: the capability itself works correctly and returns real, well-formed data (verdict is not BLOCKED or UNVERIFIED — a non-empty, specifically-matched collection was returned and paging was cross-checked against a known total), but the declared schema and the actual response body disagree on eight fields (one missing, seven extra), so DRIFT rather than PASS.
